facts.fact: Ila carries an iron survey spike as long as her forearm with a welded ring in the head, used to hold a chain; with Kunal's knife she chips sounding holes through the ice.
facts.why: needed because the beat has her sound the Drum with an iron spike and his knife.

facts.fact: The second tarn is called the Drum by Neshar families ('the heartbeat of the valley', per Kunal's father).
facts.why: needed because the outline names the second tarn the Drum; Kunal supplies the night's name.

facts.fact: Ila's ice rule of thumb: a pair with packs needs eight fingers of ice, three people twelve. Readings on the Drum range from seven to fourteen fingers.
facts.why: needed to give the thickness counts and the pair-but-not-three markings.
